sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Talence, next to Bordeaux's university campuses, regulates on-street parking in two paid zones and blue zones; the commune's own pages say eight blue zones in one place and seven in two others. Checks run from 9am to 7pm Monday to Saturday, suspended from 14 July to 15 August, and permits are handled online [0]. In blue zones everyone gets 1h30 free with a disc, residents get free rights for up to two vehicles per household and visitor passes are free for 35 days a year [1]. In paid zones everyone gets 1h30 free, and after that the tariff applies from the first quarter hour to the whole parked time; the commune's page gives no hourly rates [2]. A December 2024 guide gives a resident's first vehicle a free two-year subscription in paid zones and a paid one for the second vehicle, and says electric, hybrid and LPG vehicles can take a free green subscription [3]. The post-parking charge is 25 euros, or 17 if paid within 5 days, and a visitor day costs 2 euros in paid zones [4]. Professional subscriptions cost 120 euros a year, 40 a quarter or 20 a month, though the slide does not name the zone and the file dates from December 2024 [5]. A July 2025 map shows eight blue zones, A to H, with an extension marked for the last quarter of 2025; it does not say whether this was done [6]. The metropolitan low-emission zone bars only unclassified vehicles, and Arts et Métiers is not among the 11 park-and-rides they may use [13].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The Médoquine rail halt reopened on 21 September 2025. A press kit gives a multimodal hub there, scheduled for spring and end 2026, with 55 spaces for cars, motorbikes, car-share and taxis and 260 bike spaces, as plans; a Bus Express line to Pellegrin hospital, Talence-Thouars and Gradignan-Malartic is planned for early 2028 [15]. Talence reports 9 sites with 22 public charge points, run by Bordeaux Métropole, with three sites added this year (the page gives no year) [16]. Metropolis-wide, charging is billed at 0.38 euro per kWh, plus 4 euros an hour after four hours on slow sockets, waived from 11pm to 8am [17]. A university page of February 2024 says a parking study found the estate's 11,000 spaces largely oversized, with more than 4,000 free at the busiest time; it does not name the communes, so the figures cannot be attributed to Talence alone [14].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Talence lists public car parks of 35 to 90 spaces: Joliot-Curie, Espeleta and Notre-Dame at 35 each, Cours Gambetta at 53, all paid, and the Thouars sports ground at 90, free. The covered Talence 7e Art car park is run by Metpark [7]; its open-data record shows 321 spaces, with two hours free, 4.50 euros for three hours and 15 euros for 24 hours [8]. The Arts et Métiers park-and-ride is the unclear case. TBM's list describes it as open to all, with 593 spaces, but gives no live status [9]. A lifestyle site reported that the metropolis closed it indefinitely from 24 January 2026 after a safety inspection [10], while the metropolitan open-data record, updated on 21 October 2026, shows it as free with 590 spaces and a live counter, which suggests it reopened, though we found no announcement [11]. Talence's own page gives 199 spaces, so capacity is also unclear [12].

Our data cover Arts et Métiers, with a feed capacity of 590 spaces, for 27 days since 24 September 2026. Occupancy averaged about 17% on weekdays and 6% at weekends, with a peak of 90% on a Wednesday afternoon. We cannot tell from the feed alone whether the site was fully open throughout. The other car parks are not in our data.
